content: The interaction between glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and other drugs involves complex mechanisms, primarily mediated by the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter, hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, and inhibition of organic anion-transporting polypeptides (OATP1B1/OATP1B3) or breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP). Below are the detailed interactions: 1. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and paliperidone: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the plasma levels or effects of paliperidone by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Pantoprazole and glecaprevir/pibrentasvir: Pantoprazole increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by reducing its metabolism. Similarly, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases pantoprazole levels through other mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and pazopanib: Pazopanib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir also increases pazopanib levels through other mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Pentobarbital and glecaprevir/pibrentasvir: Pentobarbital decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may reduce therapeutic efficacy. Caution and monitoring are required. 5. Phenobarbital and glecaprevir/pibrentasvir: Phenobarbital reduces glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Pioglitazone and glecaprevir/pibrentasvir: Pioglitazone increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and pitavastatin: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases pitavastatin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1, which may elevate the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. Use the lowest approved dose of pitavastatin, and if a higher dose is necessary, assess the risk/benefit ratio. 8. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and pravastatin: Pravastatin levels are increased by glecaprevir/pibrentasvir due to OATP1B1 inhibition, raising the risk of myopathy. Reduce the pravastatin dose by 50% if co-administered. 9. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and rosuvastatin: Rosuvastatin levels are elevated by glecaprevir/pibrentasvir through OATP1B1 inhibition, increasing the risk of myopathy. Do not exceed 10 mg/day of rosuvastatin when co-administered. 10. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and rifabutin/rifapentine: Rifabutin and rifapentine decrease glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing therapeutic efficacy. Caution and monitoring are required. 11. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and tenofovir (AF/DF): Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases tenofovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor for potential toxicities. 12. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and testosterone: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases testosterone levels by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and statins (general): Increased statin concentrations due to OATP1B1 inhibition may elevate the risk of myopathy. Adjust statin doses accordingly and monitor closely. 14. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and CYP3A4 substrates: Drugs that induce or inhibit CYP3A4 can significantly alter glecaprevir/pibrentasvir plasma concentrations, affecting therapeutic efficacy or increasing toxicity. Adjust dosages and monitor as clinically indicated. 15. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and P-gp/BCRP substrates: Co-administration with P-gp or BCRP inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir or other substrates, necessitating dose adjustments and close monitoring. 16.
